defects.detail: The white toilet seat is drawn as a near-vertical hoop facing the viewer, framing the globe through its hole, rather than as a flat Saturn-like ring circling around the globe. The lower half of the globe bulges below it, so the combined object partly reads as a toilet bowl.

attempts.visual: 1990s risograph print in fluorescent orange and teal on warm cream paper, visible print grain and slight overprint misregistration. Centre stage: a low, flat, rectangular wooden theatre platform, seen from the front. Standing on the platform is one large spherical globe — a perfect round ball with simple black continent outlines and a few latitude/longitude grid lines, half coloured orange and half teal. Encircling the globe's middle, tilted slightly like a halo in three-quarter perspective, is ONE single chunky toilet seat and nothing else: a thick, solid off-white oval donut-shaped ring with a smooth rounded front, a straighter flattened back edge with two small hinge bumps, visible thickness/side wall, and a large oval hole in its centre through which the globe passes. The seat is a solid object casting a slight shadow on the globe; it must not be thin, flat, double, or made of concentric planetary bands. At the top left and top right corners, one black theatre spotlight fixture each, angled inward, casting two wide triangular cones of light — fluorescent orange from the left, teal from the right — crossing behind the globe. Dark teal stage curtains frame only the far left and far right edges. Across the entire bottom foreground, a row of solid-black audience silhouettes seen from behind: backs of heads, shoulders and raised arms with open hands, some heads tilted back in laughter, with no facial features, no eyes or mouths, and no individual clothing detail. No text, letters, numbers, logos or signage anywhere.

defects.detail: The key metaphor does not read: the object around the globe is a thin, flat, elliptical Saturn-style ring with small clasps at the sides. It has no thick toilet-seat rim, no recognisable oval seat shape, hinge, or lid, so it reads as a planet ring rather than a white toilet seat.
